deep.reconstruction:
There is essentially no mathematics on this page. Folio 29v is mostly the recto (29r) showing through the paper, so the writing appears mirror-reversed. Read against the transcription of 29r, the ink lines are a library loan slip: 'Poggendorff. Annalen der Physik und Chemie. 3. Reihe Bd 11. 1847. nebst Tafeln zu [Bd. 10-12 struck out] 3. Reihe Bd 10-12'. The mirrored lower-right line 'Oct. 30. 54.' dates the slip to 30 October 1854, Riemann's first semester as Privatdozent. The lower-left signature reads 'B Riemann, Dr. ph. (Barfüßerstr. ...)', i.e. his Göttingen address. The red mark '8 . 4' at the right and the pencilled 'a/b'-like marks next to the crosses at the top right also match the recto.

The only possibly mathematical marks are some faint pencil fractions at the left, also apparently mirrored: a lone 'a/b', then two quotients of three-term sums. The legible forms are roughly (r+p+q)/(v+t+s) and (r+b+q)/(v+t+s) (my reading; the letters are uncertain because mirroring swaps p/q and b/d), with a stroke drawn through them, plus a struck-through diagonal line above. They could be a jotted ratio of sums of quantities, for example a mediant-type combination of the fractions a/b. That interpretation is entirely mine and speculative. There is no derivation, equation or result to reconstruct. The page documents Riemann borrowing Poggendorff's Annalen, presumably for his physics interests (electrodynamics, Nobili rings) in 1854.
errors: No mathematical steps on the page, so there is nothing to check for errors.

The machine transcription treats the text as original verso writing. It is mostly show-through of the recto loan slip, so readings such as 'Theorie der ... 3 Stück' should be 'Annalen der Physik und Chemie 3 Reihe'.

checkable.sympy: import sympy as s; a,b,c,d=s.symbols('a b c d',positive=True); s.simplify((a+c)/(b+d) - a/b - (b*c-a*d)/(b*(b+d)))==0
checkable.asserts: Speculative interpretation only: the mediant (a+c)/(b+d) differs from a/b by (bc-ad)/(b(b+d)). For positive quantities it therefore lies between a/b and c/d.
